repairs.title: SGLang Ascend GDN prefill swaps recurrent-state axes

title.en: SGLang Ascend GDN prefill swaps recurrent-state axes

summary.en: Baseline differs on 480/704 paired elements. Candidate matches all 704 paired elements.

settings.fixture: deterministic synthetic tensors without model weights

problem.summary: SGLang Ascend GDN prefill swaps recurrent-state axes
problem.trigger: Packed lengths 65 and 3, two heads, square K=V=4, with attention output, final recurrent state and chunk snapshots.
problem.expected: Every paired observation matches its fixture reference exactly.
problem.observed: Baseline differs on 480/704 paired elements. Candidate matches all 704 paired elements.

cause.summary: The wrapper passes [V,K] pool state directly to the chunk operation whose contract uses [K,V]. Square state dimensions allow the wrong orientation to continue silently.

repair.summary: Transpose state at entry to the chunk operation and restore the pool orientation on returned final and chunk states.

validation.scope: Packed lengths 65 and 3, two heads, square K=V=4, with attention output, final recurrent state and chunk snapshots.
checks: Both arms report zero nonfinite elements.
The same fixture and exact reference criterion are used for both revisions.
remaining: The external NPU chunk operation is replaced by a CPU delta-rule implementation. Coverage is the extracted Python wrapper with square state and FP32 synthetic inputs.

evidence.label: CPU fixture measurements and upstream provenance

notes: Retained measured result from a minimal reproduction of a documented upstream change.

summary.en: Baseline differs on 772/3208 paired elements. Candidate matches all 3208 paired elements.

problem.summary: SGLang Ascend MLA cache includes invalid tokens between request prefixes
problem.trigger: DCP=1, page size four, with ND/NZ layouts and mixed [3,0,5,1] or page-aligned [4,0,8,4] prefix lengths.
problem.expected: Every paired observation matches its fixture reference exactly.
problem.observed: Baseline differs on 772/3208 paired elements. Candidate matches all 3208 paired elements.

cause.summary: Whole-page gathering leaves invalid tail rows between logical prefixes while the attention consumer uses cumulative logical lengths.

repair.summary: Compact latent and RoPE cache rows using valid token indices before the attention boundary.

validation.scope: DCP=1, page size four, with ND/NZ layouts and mixed [3,0,5,1] or page-aligned [4,0,8,4] prefix lengths.
checks: Both arms report zero nonfinite elements.
The same fixture and exact reference criterion are used for both revisions.
remaining: The extracted Python cache path uses synthetic CPU tensors and metadata. Ascend FIA, distributed DCP and full-model results are outside these measurements.

evidence.label: CPU fixture measurements and upstream provenance

notes: Retained measured result from a minimal reproduction of a documented upstream change.

title.en: vLLM-Ascend leaves DeepSeek V4 attention sinks stale after reload

summary.en: Baseline differs on 144/144 paired elements. Candidate matches all 144 paired elements.

settings.fixture: deterministic synthetic tensors without model weights

problem.summary: vLLM-Ascend leaves DeepSeek V4 attention sinks stale after reload
problem.trigger: Two synthetic attention-sink updates through target, MTP and DSpark loaders with TP2 rank-local and DSA context-parallel layouts.
problem.expected: Every paired observation matches its fixture reference exactly.
problem.observed: Baseline differs on 144/144 paired elements. Candidate matches all 144 paired elements.

cause.summary: The original attention-sink loading branch bypasses the configured weight loader, preventing reload updates from being captured for replay.

repair.summary: Use the configured parameter loader after selecting the correct rank-local or full sink tensor.

validation.scope: Two synthetic attention-sink updates through target, MTP and DSpark loaders with TP2 rank-local and DSA context-parallel layouts.
checks: Both arms report zero nonfinite elements.
The same fixture and exact reference criterion are used for both revisions.
remaining: The loader paths run on CPU with a sink-only deferred replay and a cold-load control. The model checkpoint, complete native reload and service output were outside this fixture.

evidence.label: CPU fixture measurements and upstream provenance

notes: Retained measured result from a minimal reproduction of a documented upstream change.

repairs.title: MindSpeed TE sequence-parallel column linear omits inline bias

title.en: MindSpeed TE sequence-parallel column linear omits inline bias

summary.en: Baseline differs on 16/224 paired elements. Candidate matches all 224 paired elements.

settings.fixture: deterministic synthetic tensors without model weights

problem.summary: MindSpeed TE sequence-parallel column linear omits inline bias
problem.trigger: BF16 forward and backward with two simulated TP ranks and absent, zero, inline nonzero and deferred bias controls.
problem.expected: Every paired observation matches its fixture reference exactly.
problem.observed: Baseline differs on 16/224 paired elements. Candidate matches all 224 paired elements.

cause.summary: The all-gather matmul receives no bias and the sequence-parallel wrapper fails to add its supplied bias to the returned output.

repair.summary: Add the supplied bias once after all-gather matmul. The outer wrapper continues to return deferred bias separately.

validation.scope: BF16 forward and backward with two simulated TP ranks and absent, zero, inline nonzero and deferred bias controls.
checks: Both arms report zero nonfinite elements.
The same fixture and exact reference criterion are used for both revisions.
remaining: The real Python wrapper and autograd code run with simulated CPU collectives. FP8, native communication, MC2 and model training are outside these measurements.

evidence.label: CPU fixture measurements and upstream provenance

notes: Retained measured result from a minimal reproduction of a documented upstream change.

repairs.title: MindSpeed CP1 packed MTP misinterprets cumulative sequence endpoints

title.en: MindSpeed CP1 packed MTP misinterprets cumulative sequence endpoints

summary.en: Baseline differs on 92/115 paired elements. Candidate matches all 115 paired elements.

settings.fixture: deterministic synthetic tensors without model weights

problem.summary: MindSpeed CP1 packed MTP misinterprets cumulative sequence endpoints
problem.trigger: CP1 with one or two packed segments over six tokens; compares labels, loss mask, valid-token count, loss, logits gradient and shared attention endpoints.
problem.expected: Every paired observation matches its fixture reference exactly.
problem.observed: Baseline differs on 92/115 paired elements. Candidate matches all 115 paired elements.

cause.summary: The CP1 path interprets cumulative end offsets as though they were a zero-prefixed boundary list.

repair.summary: Recognize the endpoint representation and include the first logical segment when shifting without changing the shared attention endpoints.

validation.scope: CP1 with one or two packed segments over six tokens; compares labels, loss mask, valid-token count, loss, logits gradient and shared attention endpoints.
checks: Both arms report zero nonfinite elements.
The same fixture and exact reference criterion are used for both revisions.
remaining: CPU execution covers the pinned shift wrapper and a synthetic loss only. This fixture does not run context-parallel communication or a full training model.

evidence.label: CPU fixture measurements and upstream provenance

notes: Retained measured result from a minimal reproduction of a documented upstream change.

repairs.title: MindSpeed-LLM reuses padding zeros in cached GPT loss masks

title.en: MindSpeed-LLM reuses padding zeros in cached GPT loss masks

summary.en: Baseline differs on 4/16 paired elements. Candidate matches all 16 paired elements.

settings.fixture: deterministic synthetic tensors without model weights

problem.summary: MindSpeed-LLM reuses padding zeros in cached GPT loss masks
problem.trigger: Pinned MindSpeed-LLM and Megatron Core paths with a padded sample, a following unpadded sample, a batch-padding sample and cached-mask inspection.
problem.expected: Every paired observation matches its fixture reference exactly.
problem.observed: Baseline differs on 4/16 paired elements. Candidate matches all 16 paired elements.

cause.summary: Sample-specific padding mutates the reusable loss-mask tensor, leaking zeros into later samples.

repair.summary: Keep the reusable mask separate and apply sample-specific padding to the sample mask.

validation.scope: Pinned MindSpeed-LLM and Megatron Core paths with a padded sample, a following unpadded sample, a batch-padding sample and cached-mask inspection.
checks: Both arms report zero nonfinite elements.
The same fixture and exact reference criterion are used for both revisions.
remaining: The production wrapper and Megatron mask code execute on CPU; document reads use synthetic tokens and no full dataloader or training step is run.

evidence.label: CPU fixture measurements and upstream provenance

notes: Retained measured result from a minimal reproduction of a documented upstream change.
